The test image shows split soybean stems revealing the internal pith. Key features:
- Stems split longitudinally, showing interior pith
- Dark/black granular material inside the pith (top stem)
- Bleached/whitish external stem tissue
- Soil background context (crown/root area)

The dark granular material inside the pith strongly suggests either **Charcoal Rot** (microsclerotia) or **Brown Stem Rot** (brown pith). Let me check references for both, plus two other candidates.

Brown Stem Rot reference matches well - split stem with brown/dark internal pith. Very similar composition to test image. Let me check one more Charcoal Rot reference showing the split stem, and one more class.
Charcoal Rot reference shows distinctive black microsclerotia dots in stem tissue. The test image's dark black pith mass aligns with this. Let me check one final reference.

**Analysis summary:**

- Test image: Split soybean stems on soil, revealing internal pith. Upper stem shows dense black internal discoloration. External stem tissue is pale/bleached white.
- Brown_Stem_Rot reference (103): Very similar split-stem setup with dark-brown pith — close match in composition.
- Charcoal_Rot reference (116): Shows black microsclerotia dots in stem tissue — the black color in the test image aligns with this.
- SDS reference: Field view, not comparable.

**Key distinction:** Brown Stem Rot turns the pith brown; Charcoal Rot turns it dark gray-black with microsclerotia. The test image shows distinctly black (not brown) internal pith with the bleached exterior — this combination is the hallmark of Charcoal Rot (*Macrophomina phaseolina*).
